newsitem.title: FRANCE: Analysts to stay mum on France Telecom.
newsitem.headline: Analysts to stay mum on France Telecom.

text.p: Financial analysts who attended a France Telecom information meeting on its pending partial privatisation are not allowed to publish their value estimates until after April 11, a company spokeswoman said on Friday.
"It is as frustrating for me as for journalists," an analyst at a big investment house in London said. "We can only use our calculations internally."

Analysts employed by banks advising France Telecom or the French state cannot make their valuations publicly. Their work will be sent to the independent Privatisation Commission, which will set a minimum value at which the government will be allowed to go ahead with the sale.
The rules on non-publication of valuations are common practice and were also used in the Deutsche Telekom flotation in November 1996.
France Telecom on Thursday hosted a meeting with some 250 financial analysts from all over the world to give them information to help them make their calculations.
"They received the same information as we made available to journalists at the news conference (on Wednesday)," a company spokeswoman said.
The French government will sell between 30 and 50 billion francs in shares in France Telecom in an operation to start on the evening of May 5 with the announcement of a price range.

From May 6 to May 26, private investors can reserve shares through their banks. On the evening of May 26, the final price will be announced and the market float will start on May 27. First share trading in New York and Paris is set for June 9.
The big question for analysts is to put a value on the company to judge whether the final share price set by the government is attractive or not.
Investment banks all have their favourite models and methods for valuing companies based on the capacity to generate cash and profits and on the outlook for the companies' markets.
The findings are compared to data for peer companies to establish ratings and assess relative market value. Absolute market value will also reflect the general price level on stock markets.

Up to now, estimates for France Telecom's value have been in a very wide range between 100 and 200 billion francs, with a Barclays de Zoete Wedd (BZW) study in July 1996 arriving at a central value of 147 billion francs. The BZW study is one of the rare detailed published reports on the company, using 1997 valuations as a base.
In July, BZW put the average 1997 price earnings ratio (P/E) for European telecommunications companies at 11.5. According to Reuters Securities 3000 this stood on March 21, 1997, at 17.

Price/earnings ratios are the crudest possible valuation measures -- and BZW used far more sophisticated yardsticks -- but a rise in the P/E of more than 50 percent since July indicates that the valuation could be revised upwards.

France Telecom chairman Michel Bon on Wednesday said he expected a "stabilisation" in 1997 of the pre-exceptional result at its record 1996 level of 14.5 billion francs. A company official said this meant a net income of at least 10 billion.
Using the crude P/E valuation, the would give France Telecom a value of more than 170 billion francs, or 170 francs per share.
